title: Length of the Longest Alphabetical Continuous Substring
summary: An alphabetical continuous string is a substring of consecutive letters in the alphabet.
statement: An alphabetical continuous string is a substring of consecutive letters in the alphabet. Given a string s, find the length of the longest such substring.
constraints: A substring is alphabetically continuous when every next character is exactly one letter after the previous.
The substring must be contiguous and nonempty.
hints: Track the continuous run length ending at each character.
Extend it when ord(current)=ord(previous)+1; otherwise reset it to one.
Every qualifying substring ends at some position and its longest possible start is represented by that position’s run value.
editorial: Every qualifying substring ends at some position and its longest possible start is represented by that position’s run value.

tests.explanation: The longest continuous part is ab, with length two.
Every step advances one letter, so the whole length-five string qualifies.
